issue: UK access-control rows cite guidance that predates the 2018 MDP restructure
current_resolution: OPEN, and self-inflicted on 2026-11-06. UK-G2 is Guidance Notes Issue Six of 30 March 2015. It describes the PRE-2018 regime: premium subscription film services capped at BBFC 15, pay-per-view at 18, the whole framing being 'mandatory restricted access'. Ofcom's statement of 5 November 2018 (UK-M1) restructured this, extending MANDATORY DAYTIME PROTECTION to scheduled television channels and permitting films up to BBFC 18 at any time of day behind the gate. So these two rows rest on guidance written about a rule structure that no longer stands.
action_required: EXACTLY the C-09 pattern, committed hours after the C-09 lesson was written down: wording that is internally coherent, corroborated by other sources of the same vintage, and quietly superseded by an amending instrument nobody read. Corroboration cannot catch this - only reading the amending instrument can. Rows demoted to unverified rather than deleted, because the substance (a gate the viewer can switch off is not a gate) is probably still correct. ACTION: re-derive both from the current Section One text plus UK-M1, then restore to approved. UK-G2 should be re-dated or replaced with current guidance. GENERAL LESSON FOR TASK 2: every source needs an 'amended by' field, and no row should reach approved while citing guidance older than the most recent amendment to the rule it interprets.

issue: Only Code Sections One and Two had been reviewed. Sections Three to Ten were assumed irrelevant to age ratings and broadcast hours.
current_resolution: CLOSED 2026-11-06, after the first answer was WRONG. I originally scoped the Code with one test - the phrase 'significant numbers of children', which is how Rules 1.27 and 4.7 key their child-audience restrictions - and concluded Sections Three and Five-Ten were out of scope. Section Three does not contain that phrase, so the test cleared it. But Rules 3.2 (hate speech) and 3.3 (abusive or derogatory treatment) are permitted 'except where it is justified by the context', and 'context' is Section Two's DEFINED term whose third factor is the TIME OF BROADCAST. So a Section Three judgment can turn on the hour. The test could not see that, so it was the wrong test, and everything it cleared was unproven rather than cleared. Added UK-HAT-001 and UK-HAT-002.
action_required: THE RIGHT TEST IS TWO DOORS, NOT ONE: (a) 'significant numbers of children may be expected to be watching' -> Rules 1.27, 4.7; (b) 'justified by the context', which imports the time-of-broadcast factor -> Sections One, Two, Three. Sections Five-Eight instead use 'editorially justified', a narrower test that does NOT import the context definition and so never turns on the hour - verified against the live Section Five page, which uses 'editorially justified' only at Rule 5.3, uses 'justified by the context' in no rule, and mentions neither children nor the watershed nor any time of day. Sections Nine and Ten govern commercial references; Section Ten does use a context test, but for programmes about commercial companies - a sponsorship question, not a content-harm question - so it is out of scope on the same reasoning that excludes the ASA/BCAP advertising codes. IN SCOPE: Sections One, Two, Three, Four. LESSON: a single lexical test is not a scoping method. Any future country should be scoped by enumerating the escape clauses, not by searching for one phrase.

issue: Is broadcast-code-full.pdf (UK-S0) a usable substitute for the per-section HTML? It is one file covering all ten sections, which is operationally attractive.
current_resolution: NO - CLOSED 2026-11-06. It is the January 2019 print edition and predates the Code in force. Ofcom's 31 Dec 2020 statement states the Code 'is now published on the Ofcom website and is no longer available in print', so no consolidated PDF has been maintained since. The Code in force covers programmes broadcast on or after 23:00 on 31 Dec 2020; the 31 Dec 2020 amendments changed the Section Three hate-speech definition and Section Nine product placement plus minor updates; and Sections One and Two were revised again on 2023-03-16 and 2024-02-19. UK-S0 demoted to optional/original_superseded.
action_required: None. But note the near-miss: an earlier version of this repo recorded UK-S0 as CONTAINING UK-S1/S2/S4 and advised fetching it to save three downloads. Following that advice would have pinned the UK rules to 2019 text and silently dropped the 2023 and 2024 revisions - the same class of error as C-09, where an outdated edition got treated as current. The lesson is that a bundle is only a shortcut if its currency is established FIRST, and 'it is a single tidy file' is exactly the kind of convenience that discourages checking.
